data.body:
Ownership-visibility archaeology (2026-09-06): Gerrit offers useful metadata but not true per-session ownership under one account. Native surfaces found: topics (`PUT /changes/{id}/topic`), hashtags (`POST /changes/{id}/hashtags`), ReviewInput `tag` on change messages/reviews, attention set (user/account oriented, weak under a shared service user), and custom keyed values (`/custom_keyed_values`, documented as small external-system IDs). Repo precedent: darksome-starry-sable used Gerrit as source of truth and keyed transient markers by `change_id + patchset_SHA`; dismal-uncheerful-rockrat required fresh Verified on the exact patchset SHA before submit and used topic as `stack_id`. CONTRIBUTING.md and ADR 0047 record the current Rebase-If-Necessary + plain Submit model.

Submit-safety finding: Gerrit REST supports the exact CAS shape we need. `GET /changes/{id}/revisions/current` returns RevisionInfo including the current commit SHA/ref. More importantly, `POST /changes/{id}/revisions/{revision-id}/submit` submits a specific revision and returns 409 Conflict if that revision is not current (“revision ... is not current revision”). That is a native submit-if-current precondition; no global serialization required.

Recommended design: on push/comment, stamp session identity as a hashtag or custom keyed value (e.g. `rebar-session=<session-id>`; hashtag if UI visibility matters, custom keyed value if machine-readability matters), and before submit always re-read current revision + live labels, then call revision-scoped submit on the SHA whose votes were inspected. If the current SHA differs or revision-submit returns 409, refuse loudly: another session changed/rebased it. Verdict: resolved-with-evidence / recommended design; needs user sign-off only for the metadata vehicle (hashtag vs custom keyed value vs both), not for the safety guard.
